s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive spinal cord syndrome with acute worsening of motor weakness
salient_findings: Gradually progressive motor weakness of the left lower extremity
Acute worsening of weakness with inability to stand or walk without assistance
Spastic paraparesis with increased reflexes and sustained clonus
key_facts: 68-year-old retired man with no prior medical history
Two months of dorsal spine pain
Progressive motor weakness of the left lower extremity
Acute worsening of weakness one week before admission
No history of trauma
Spastic paraparesis with weakness of the quadriceps, hamstrings, ankle dorsiflexors, and toe extensors on the left
Increased patellar and ankle jerks with sustained clonus at the left ankle
Bilateral Babinski signs
Superficial hypoesthesia present below the T7 level
Bladder and bowel function preserved
Magnetic resonance imaging showed a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass posterolateral to the right side of the spinal cord at C7–T1

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with dural tail sign and heterogeneous enhancement on MRI, consistent with meningioma

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extra-axial mass with intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal on T2-weighted images, consistent with schwannoma

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive motor weakness and spinal cord compression, consistent with neurofibroma

shortlist.label: Metastatic spinal cord tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Acute worsening of motor weakness and presence of an extra-axial mass, raising concern for metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with heterogeneous enhancement on MRI, consistent with hemangioblastoma

raw.rationale: The patient's MRI shows a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with a thin rim of enhancement and no internal enhancement, which is consistent with a meningioma. Meningiomas are also known to cause spinal cord compression and deformity, leading to the patient's symptoms of progressive motor weakness and spastic paraparesis.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically associated with nerve roots and would more likely cause radiculopathy rather than the patient's presentation of spastic paraparesis and cord compression.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are also associated with nerve roots and are more commonly seen in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1, which is not mentioned in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Metastatic spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: Metastatic tumors would more likely have a heterogeneous appearance on MRI and may have a more rapid onset of symptoms, which is not consistent with the patient's two-month history of progressive weakness.

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Hemangioblastomas are typically associated with a more heterogeneous appearance on MRI due to their vascular nature and would more likely have a cystic component, which is not seen in the patient's MRI.
